context: US flight route bundling map showing 50 airports and 200 routes across 5 regions, with edge bundling controlled by a tension slider and hover-to-highlight interaction
first_impression: The visualization failed to render entirely in the screenshot — only the title and tension slider are visible against a blank dark canvas, likely because the external us-atlas CDN fetch failed at capture time.
what_works: The code design is cognitively sound: 5-color regional palette stays well within the 8-hue warning threshold, and the hover-to-highlight interaction (dimming non-connected routes to near-invisible) is a strong technique for managing 200-route density without overwhelming the viewer.
what_doesnt: The visualization has a hard runtime dependency on an external CDN fetch (us-atlas topojson) with no fallback — a single network failure produces a completely blank canvas with no error state; additionally, with tension at 0.15 (nearly straight lines) and 200 routes, the default state before hover interaction would likely read as a dense hairball over the map without the bundling effect doing meaningful separation.
